assessment: Using advanced live brain imaging techniques, the authors studied the activities of neurons in the primary motor cortex of mice during a classical conditional task, in which a tone is paired with a water reward. They found that distinct types of neurons respond differently to the auditory cue or the reward, and the responses evolve differentially as learning proceeds. This work reveals an interesting role of the motor cortex beyond its well-recognized function in motor control and suggests distinct functions of pyramidal neurons as well as various interneurons in reinforcement learning.
